dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Minnesota Vikings Face Defensive Breakdown in Week 11 Matchup Against 49ers
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: At 7-2, Minnesota faced heavy pressure against San Francisco's top-ranked offense, struggling to contain quick underneath spacing concepts despite sustaining early time of possession. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores saw his unit yield unprecedented first-half scoring output against Brock Purdy.
bullets: San Francisco generated 8.7 yards per play in the first half with zero turnovers, scoring more first-half points than Minnesota had surrendered in any single game this season, as reported by [Ben Goessling](https://bsky.app/profile/bengoessling.bsky.social/post/3n2x3vs624b2k) and [Andrew Krammer](https://bsky.app/profile/andrewkrammer.bsky.social/post/3n2x3zrvv3k2x).

Quarterback Kirk Cousins connected with receiver Justin Jefferson on a 29-yard deep pass during first-half offensive action, per [vikings.com Video](https://www.vikings.com/video/kirk-cousins-justin-jefferson-29-yard-completion-catch-49ers).

Linebacker Eric Wilson notched a sack on a zero-blitz, but 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy retaliated with high efficiency, completing a touchdown pass to George Kittle over Harrison Smith, detailed by [Andrew Krammer](https://bsky.app/profile/andrewkrammer.bsky.social/post/3n2x2evfszc2n).

Kicker Will Reichard missed a field goal attempt wide left on an opening drive, handing San Francisco short-field starting position at their own 45-yard line, per [Ben Goessling](https://bsky.app/profile/bengoessling.bsky.social/post/3n2wysfnsep2p).
